elements.label: EXAMPLE 6.4
elements.title: Discrete Logistic Regression Model Example for Graduation Probability
elements.details:
| Variable | Description | Probability |
|----------|-------------|-------------|
| p1       | Probability of graduating if "in-state" is false (0) | 0.3 |
| p2       | Probability of graduating if "in-state" is true (1)  | 0.75 |

Additional calculations:
- logit(p1) = ln(0.3 / (1 - 0.3)) = ln(0.4286) = -0.847
- logit(p2) = ln(0.75 / (1 - 0.75)) = ln(3.000) = 1.099
- a = logit(p1) = -0.847
- b = logit(p2) - logit(p1) = 1.099 - (-0.847) = 1.946

Final logistic regression model:

f(x) = 1 / (1 + e^(-(-0.847 + 1.946x))) = 1 / (1 + e^(0.847 - 1.946x))
elements.summary: This example shows how to build a discrete logistic regression model to predict graduation likelihood based on whether a student is in-state or out-of-state, using given probabilities and the logit function.
